findings.title: Stale active descendant
findings.body:
`aria-activedescendant` is now skipped whenever `keyMods.ctrlCmd` is held, but nothing re-syncs it when the modifier is released. Quick Open supports keyboard navigation while Ctrl/Cmd is held: repeatedly pressing Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) moves through the list via `quickOpenNavigateNext`.

During that navigation, focus changes are never exposed to assistive technology. The screen reader stays silent, and `aria-activedescendant` keeps pointing at the old item after Ctrl is released. Accepting with Enter then picks an item the screen reader user never heard announced.

Suggested fixes:
- Narrow the guard to the case where Ctrl was pressed with no navigation.
- Or update `aria-activedescendant` once the modifier is released.

findings.title: Same regression in tree
findings.body: The tree `onDidChangeFocus` handler has the same Ctrl/Cmd guard. Navigating with Ctrl/Cmd held (e.g., Ctrl+P cycling) won't update `aria-activedescendant` for tree-based quick picks either, so focused items aren't announced.

findings.title: Non-verifying test
findings.body:
The test ends with `assert.ok(true)` and never checks the `aria-label` value or whether redundant `setAttribute` calls are avoided. It would pass even if the new dedup logic were removed or broken.

It should assert the input element's `aria-label` after each placeholder change. It could also spy on `setAttribute` to confirm the same-value update is skipped.
